prose_updates.related_work: HanOwusuShin2026 is the closest same-estimand paper, but its decision action is a full vector of pairwise rankings under additive pairwise regret, whereas the headline mechanism game here selects one welfare-maximizing policy under simple regret. HanOwusuShin2026 is also the closest same-target paper: its Appendix-B Eq. (S1), pp. 40--44, uses the Horvitz--Thompson normalization \(1/(Cp_k)\) and a within-label likelihood ratio; the exact comparison theorem derives its influence variance and strictly refines it through cross-label assignment calibration. HiranoPorter2009 supplies the limit-experiment architecture, but the all-rule nuisance-deletion theorem and legal observed-law exact-hit tangent are specific to this model. BairdBohrenMcIntoshOzler2018 makes saturation shares a design object under a power criterion rather than optimized facewise simple regret. Joo2025 informs the static Gaussian selector; the contribution here is its coupling to the exact-hit polytope, a general certified outer-design procedure over the exact-hit polytope, and calibrated cluster-data transfer, not a new generic Gaussian minimax construction. Kato2026, arXiv:2506.24007v6 dated 25 July 2026, is Masahiro Kato's adaptive sequential best-arm comparator and only informs the certification architecture. LoombaEckles2026 informs score projection under structured interference. JiangImaiMalani2023 and MogstadRomanoShaikhWilhelm2024 inform the supporting covariance and rank-inversion results. ChanNakamuraSakaiForastiere2023 is nonarchival prior use of cross-label information for a different hypothetical-allocation target. EggerHaushoferMiguelNiehausWalker2022 supplies the prospective Kenya saturation-design consumer. Within the accepted experimentation bank, \texttt{exp\_bipartite\_minimax\_design/v1}, especially \(\texttt{thm:convex-design}\) and \(\texttt{thm:heterogeneity-separation}\), optimizes heterogeneous intervention-unit Bernoulli propensities for a graph-only conservative bipartite H\'ajek-variance envelope; it does not compare cluster-label Bernoulli exact-hit information with exact-count assignment or study tie-face best-policy simple regret. The accepted \texttt{exp\_rollout\_chebyshev\_minimax/tv\_envelope\_rollout\_design} results \(\texttt{thm:tv-envelope-design}\) and \(\texttt{thm:chebyshev-minimax}\) select rollout measurement fractions and unbiased weights for a total-variation-envelope total-treatment-effect extrapolation problem; they have neither a Bernoulli miss-hit versus exact-count comparison nor a facewise regret-ratio equality criterion. The accepted \texttt{exp\_snipe\_degree\_frontier/v1} result \(\texttt{thm:bounded-outcome-degree-frontier}\) establishes a degree-sensitive minimax mean-squared-error frontier for total treatment effect under fixed unit Bernoulli randomization and \(\beta\)-order neighborhood interference, attained by clipped SNIPE; it does not optimize a cluster-label mixture against an exact-count benchmark or analyze local best-policy loss. Positively, \(\texttt{thm:mechanism-loss}\) compares two assignment mechanisms for the same exact-slice welfare-selection target through \(q=Bp\), the active hit mass \(s_A\), and the equality condition requiring support on maximum-mass columns together with an exact-count-optimal normalized active vector.

statement_notes.justification: This is the sole field-level headline: a sharp optimized information-loss frontier for the same exact-count causal target. Its non-overlap with the accepted experimentation-bank kernels is substantive: \texttt{exp\_multiarm\_secondorder\_minimax\_frontier} studies fixed-arm finite-population contrast mean-squared error and its second-order \(n^{-4/3}\) frontier, not clustered exact-slice welfare or a Bernoulli-hit versus exact-count mechanism comparison; \texttt{exp\_design\_pm1\_exactness\_boundary} certifies plus-minus-one implementability of a homophily covariance-SDP relaxation, not target-hit information or simple-regret ranking. The accepted \texttt{exp\_bipartite\_minimax\_design/v1} theorems \(\texttt{thm:convex-design}\) and \(\texttt{thm:heterogeneity-separation}\) optimize heterogeneous intervention-unit Bernoulli propensities for a graph-only conservative bipartite H\'ajek-variance envelope, not the relative information of cluster-level exact-hit mechanisms. The accepted \texttt{exp\_rollout\_chebyshev\_minimax/tv\_envelope\_rollout\_design} theorems \(\texttt{thm:tv-envelope-design}\) and \(\texttt{thm:chebyshev-minimax}\) optimize rollout measurement fractions and unbiased weights for total-variation-envelope total-treatment-effect extrapolation, not exact-hit policy selection. The accepted \texttt{exp\_snipe\_degree\_frontier/v1} theorem \(\texttt{thm:bounded-outcome-degree-frontier}\) gives a degree-sensitive minimax mean-squared-error frontier for clipped SNIPE under fixed unit Bernoulli assignment and \(\beta\)-order neighborhood interference, not a cluster-label mixture versus exact-count benchmark. In contrast, \(\texttt{thm:mechanism-loss}\) compares those two mechanisms for the same exact-slice welfare-selection target through \(q=Bp\), active hit mass \(s_A\), and the support/normalized-active-vector equality certificate.
statement_notes.gap: Prior saturation-design papers do not provide this all-rule facewise equality frontier. In particular, the accepted-bank multiarm minimax result neither has the unrestricted independent and identically distributed cluster-schedule model, the exact-count welfare estimand, nor the hit map \(q=Bp\); the accepted-bank plus-minus-one design result neither compares Bernoulli labels with complete randomization nor has a tie-face Gaussian selection game. The accepted bipartite Bernoulli-design frontier instead controls a graph-only conservative bipartite H\'ajek-variance envelope under heterogeneous intervention-unit propensities; the accepted rollout frontier instead solves a total-variation-envelope total-treatment-effect extrapolation design over measurement fractions and unbiased weights; and the accepted SNIPE frontier instead treats degree-sensitive total-treatment-effect mean-squared error under a fixed unit-Bernoulli design and \(\beta\)-order neighborhood interference. None compares cluster-label Bernoulli exact-hit information with exact-count assignment for the same exact-slice welfare target, and none supplies the facewise regret-ratio equality criterion. The gap filled by \(\texttt{thm:mechanism-loss}\) is the explicit comparison through \(q=Bp\), \(s_A\), and the condition that a Bernoulli optimizer be supported on maximum-active-hit-mass columns and induce an exact-count-optimal normalized active vector; this criterion also yields the cluster-count implication.
